item.title: Grace Has Authority
item.description:
Yesterday I wrote about grace as receiving what we do not deserve. But there is another part of grace that I think is easy to miss: grace is only as meaningful as the authority of the person giving it.

At the end of my university years I had accumulated a lot of debt. Some of it was simply the cost of living and studying; some of it, if I am honest, was not always spent particularly wisely. Either way, it was thousands and thousands of pounds, and it was mine. I had incurred it and there was no reasonable argument that somebody else should carry it for me.

item.title: Lowering the Cost of Curiosity
item.description:
I have been doing a lot of experimentation with local models recently, as have many of my colleagues. There is also a growing anticipation around the next generation of developer workstations and AI-focused boxes: machines capable of running increasingly useful models without sending every request to a SaaS platform.

It is easy to see this as another technology choice: local versus cloud, open model versus proprietary model, workstation versus API. I think the more interesting question for enterprises is economic.
